channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Rehabilitation of Athletes With Hamstring Strain Injury: SONAFE-Brazil Clinical Practice Guideline.
item.description: The National Society of Sports Physical Therapy (SONAFE-Brazil) developed a clinical practice guideline using the GRADE approach to provide evidence-based recommendations for physical therapists on interventions to improve rehabilitation outcomes in athletes with hamstring strain injury.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Association Between Early Postoperative Limb Symmetry Index Scores and 2-Year Patient-Reported Outcomes After Quadriceps Tendon Autograft ACL Reconstruction.
item.description: Early isometric quadriceps strength LSI at 3 months post-quadriceps tendon autograft ACL reconstruction (QT-ACLR) strongly predicted 2-year IKDC scores, highlighting the importance of early strength recovery for long-term outcomes.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Percutaneous Electrolysis for the Management of Musculoskeletal Disorders. A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 13 trials found that adding percutaneous electrolysis (PNE) to therapeutic exercise for tendinopathies was not superior to sham or exercise alone for pain or function. In tendinopathies, PNE combined with TE showed greater short- and medium-term pain reduction compared to dry needling plus TE, but no functional superiority. No significant differences were found between PNE and dry needling for pain or function in myofascial pain syndrome.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical performance clustering as a marker of frailty, fall risk, and cognitive health in older adults
item.description: A study of 368 older adults used unsupervised classification of 23 physical performance measures (PPMs) to identify three distinct clusters (High, Moderate, Low Physical Performance), which significantly stratified individuals by frailty and fall risk, with muscular power and joint moments being the most discriminative features.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Effects of thoracic kinesiological taping on pulmonary functions, respiratory muscle strength, and functional independence in patients with hemiplegia: a randomized controlled clinical trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=30) found that thoracic kinesiology taping (KT) combined with conventional rehabilitation significantly improved pulmonary function (FVC, FEV1, PEF, MIP, all p<0.001) and functional independence (FIM, p=0.029) in chronic post-stroke hemiplegia patients compared to sham taping, with greater changes in the KT group.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of kinesio taping and myofascial release therapy in cervicogenic headache: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=81) found that both kinesio taping (KT) and myofascial release (MFR) combined with home exercise significantly improved pain, disability, quality of life, and headache frequency in cervicogenic headache patients over 4 weeks compared to home exercise alone. MFR showed more sustained improvements in disability and physical quality of life at one-month follow-up.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Reframing hands-on musculoskeletal assessment as a measurement instrument rather than a technique debate: a theoretical framework applying COSMIN to HODA-A.
item.description: A theoretical framework proposes conceptualizing hands-on musculoskeletal examination as a clinician-reported outcome measurement process, applying COSMIN principles to enhance scientific rigor by defining constructs, content validity, and examiner calibration.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Is Reduced Spinal Range of Motion a Prognostic Factor for Pain Intensity, Disability, and Global Recovery in People With Specific or Nonspecific Spinal Pain? A Systematic Review.
item.description: A systematic review of 37 studies found very low certainty evidence, with all studies rated high risk of bias, making it unclear whether reduced spinal range of motion independently predicts pain, disability, and global recovery in individuals with specific or nonspecific spinal pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Mirror therapy versus functional electrical stimulation cycling in post-stroke lower limb rehabilitation: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: In subacute stroke, both mirror therapy and functional electrical stimulation-assisted cycling (FES-C) significantly improved lower extremity motor function (ΔFMA-LE scores: MD -2.60 for MT, MD -3.00 for FES-C, both p<0.05 vs control), with FES-C showing additional gains in Brunnstrom stage and SS-QOL.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of iTBS and rTMS Combined with Robotic Rehabilitation on Ambulation and Lower Extremity Motor Function in Chronic SCI Patients.
item.description: This single-center, single-blind RCT (n=30) found that both rTMS and iTBS combined with robotic rehabilitation improved lower-extremity motor function, SCIM III scores, and 10 MWT in chronic SCI patients, with median LEMS improvements of 4.0 and 5.0, respectively, versus 0.0 for sham, at 4-week follow-up.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Shear wave elastography for assessing lower extremity muscle stiffness after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A systematic review.
item.description: A systematic review of six studies (n=173 ACLR, n=79 controls) found that shear wave elastography (SWE) consistently detected reduced passive vastus medialis shear modulus (Hedges' g -1.10 to -1.21) and semitendinosus stiffness (g -1.29 to -1.64 after hamstring harvest) in operative limbs after ACLR, linking these deficits to quadriceps strength, knee function, and landing biomechanics.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A Return to Performance Continuum for Football (Soccer) Players After ACL Reconstruction: Bridging Rehabilitation, Return to Play and Sustained Performance.
item.description: This paper outlines a staged return-to-performance continuum for football players after ACL reconstruction, comprising structured on-field rehabilitation, return to team training, return to competitive match play, and sustained performance, underpinned by four interdependent pillars.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Can Psychological Readiness Predict Successful Return to Sports After Patellar Stabilization Surgery in Adolescent Patients? A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: In adolescent patients after patellar stabilization surgery, higher ACL-RSI scores (≥59.2) were significantly associated with successful return to sport, even after adjusting for sex.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of office-based vergence/accommodative therapy with movement for accommodative dysfunction in concussion-related convergence insufficiency: a secondary analysis of the CONCUSS randomised clinical trial
item.description: Immediate office-based vergence/accommodative therapy with movement (OBVAM) was highly effective in remediating accommodative dysfunction associated with concussion-related convergence insufficiency compared to watchful waiting.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Efficacy and evidence certainty of traditional Chinese exercises for musculoskeletal disorders: an umbrella review of meta-analyses
item.description: High-certainty evidence supports the efficacy of Traditional Chinese Exercises (TCEs), particularly Tai Chi, for musculoskeletal disorders, with optimal benefits observed from sustained interventions (≥6 months, ≥3 times/week).
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Calf Injuries: An Anatomy-Based Approach to Diagnosis, Management and Return to Sport.
item.description: This review provides an anatomy-based approach to calf injuries, emphasizing refined anatomical characterization for diagnosis, management, and return-to-sport decisions, while highlighting limitations in evidence linking specific patterns to prognosis.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Role of Psychosocial Factors in Returning to Physical Activity and Sport Among Female Football Players After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury: A Scoping Review
item.description: A scoping review identified psychosocial factors influencing return to physical activity and sport among female football players after ACL injury. Uncertainty, fear, lack of confidence, and poor social support were perceived barriers, while confidence, motivation, strong social support, and athletic identity were facilitators.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: From information to action; co-designing pain neuroscience education for adolescents with low back pain: Focus group insights.
item.description: Co-designing pain neuroscience education with adolescents experiencing low back pain revealed needs for relatable, back-specific information, practical tools, engaging formats, and easy navigation, leading to a refined prototype.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Post-concussion screen time duration and type and its association with symptom resolution in youth aged 11-17 years
item.description: Moderate daily screen time (120-240 min) in the first 3 days post-concussion in youth (11-17 years) was associated with faster symptom resolution compared to very low or high use.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Over-the-counter analgesics improve postconcussion symptoms and recovery: findings from the Concussion Assessment, Research and Education (CARE) Consortium
item.description: Over-the-counter (OTC) analgesic use after concussion was associated with a higher rate of return to unrestricted play and reduced symptom severity, with early use showing a greater benefit.
item.author: BJSM
